### `shopping_mall_low_stock_alerts`

Configuration records for low stock alerts that trigger notifications
when inventory for a product variant falls below a defined threshold.
Each alert is associated with a specific product variant and defines the
stock threshold, notification channel, and activation status.

Enables sellers to customize alert behavior for different product
variants based on business needs and inventory policies. Alerts can be
enabled/disabled to control notification frequency and reduce system
noise during promotions or sales events.

The threshold field specifies the minimum inventory level that triggers
an alert, while notification channels determine how the alert is
delivered (email, SMS, etc.). All configuration changes are tracked
through the temporal fields for audit purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_variants_id`: Product variant this alert applies to. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `threshold`
  > Minimum inventory level that triggers alert for this variant. Must be a
  > positive integer representing stock quantity.
- `notification_channel`: Preferred delivery method for alerts (e.g., 'email', 'sms', 'slack').
- `enabled`
  > Active status of this alert configuration. True = active, False =
  > disabled.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the alert configuration was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the alert configuration was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the configuration was marked for deletion (soft delete).

### `shopping_mall_inventory_logs`

Audit trail recording all inventory changes including updates,
adjustments, and stock deductions.

This table captures historical modifications to product inventory levels,
providing a complete record of stock movements for audit purposes. Each
log entry is linked to a specific product variant inventory record and
documents the nature of changes, performers, and timestamps.

The audit trail supports compliance requirements by tracking who
performed inventory operations and when, while maintaining read-only
access to historical change records.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_variant_inventories_id`
  > Related inventory variant record. {@link
  > shopping_mall_variant_inventories.id}
- `change_description`
  > Specific details of inventory change including quantities and reasons for
  > the adjustment.
- `actor_type`: User role who performed the inventory operation (seller, admin).
- `actor_id`: Identifier of the actor performing the inventory change.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the inventory activity was recorded.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the inventory activity log was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the log record was marked for deletion.

### `shopping_mall_inventory_adjustments`

Manual inventory adjustments recorded by sellers for product variants.

Tracks sellers' actions to modify product variant stock levels, capturing
the type of adjustment (increase/decrease), quantity, and business
reason. Each record links to the specific product variant and seller,
enabling audit trails and reconciliation against automatic stock updates.
Adjustments are soft-deleted to maintain historical context while
allowing content moderation for internal review processes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_variant_id`: Product variant being adjusted. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products).
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`: Seller who performed the adjustment. [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `adjustment_type`: Type of adjustment, such as 'increase' or 'decrease'.
- `quantity`
  > Magnitude of the stock change (positive for increase, negative for
  > decrease).
- `reason`
  > Business justification for the adjustment, such as 'manual stock count',
  > 'returned items', or 'trial adjustment'.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the adjustment record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the adjustment record was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the adjustment record was soft-deleted (null indicates
  > active).

### `shopping_mall_variant_inventories`

Tracks real-time stock levels and availability status for each product
variant.

Monitors inventory quantities and status changes for product variants,
enabling immediate stock updates and visibility. Each record represents a
single product variant's current inventory state, independent of other
variants. This table supports real-time inventory checks during checkout
and purchase processes.

Status values include 'in_stock', 'out_of_stock', 'low_stock', and
'discontinued'. Stock level changes are recorded as audit events in
'shopping_mall_inventory_logs' for traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_variants_id`: Reference to the product variant record. [shopping_mall_products.id](#shopping_mall_products)
- `current_stock`
  > Current available quantity of the product variant. Must be zero or
  > positive.
- `status`
  > Current inventory status. Valid values: 'in_stock', 'out_of_stock',
  > 'low_stock', 'discontinued'.
- `created_at`: When this inventory record was created.
- `updated_at`: When this inventory record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: When this inventory record was soft-deleted. Null indicates active record.

### `shopping_mall_orders`

Main order records with customer, seller, and order details.

Stores the core information about each customer's purchase including
product selection details, payment status, shipping information, and
processing status. Each order is initiated by a customer from their
profile (shopping_mall_customers) and fulfilled by a seller
(shopping_mall_sellers).

Orders contain a running status for fulfillment workflows (pending →
processing → shipped → delivered) and maintain a historical record
through the associated snapshot table. The order tracking system supports
cancellation requests and refund processing while preserving the original
order data.

The transaction amount is calculated based on product line items and
includes applicable taxes and discounts.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`: Customer who placed the order. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `shopping_mall_seller_id`: Seller who fulfilled the order. [shopping_mall_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_sellers).
- `status`: Current order status: pending, processing, shipped, delivered, cancelled.
- `total_amount`: Total amount of the order including products and applicable taxes.
- `created_at`: Order creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for order status changes.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp if order is archived.

### `shopping_mall_order_items`

Line items for each product in an order, including variant-specific
details and pricing information at the time of purchase.

Each line item represents a single product variant (SKU) purchased within
the order, maintaining historical pricing for accurate billing and audit
trails. The table associates products with orders through variants,
capturing both item quantity and price at transaction time.

Supports order fulfillment tracking and billing reconciliation while
preserving historical data integrity without redundant denormalization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `orders_id`: Order context. {@link shopping_mall_orders.id.
- `product_variants_id`: Product variant reference. {@link shopping_mall_products.id.
- `quantity`
  > Number of items ordered. Must be positive integer representing quantity
  > purchased.
- `unit_price`
  > Price per unit at time of transaction. Records historical pricing, not
  > current catalog price.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when line item was added to order.
- `updated_at`: Last timestamp when line item data was modified.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for audit trail retention.

### `shopping_mall_orders_snapshots`

Point-in-time historical records of order status changes for audit trails
and change tracking.

Captures the exact state of an order at specific moments during its
lifecycle including status, shipping details, payment information, and
associated customer/seller data. Each snapshot is generated when an order
transitions between statuses (e.g., from 'processing' to 'shipped').

Supports compliance requirements for order history analysis and dispute
resolution. Snapshots are append-only and rarely modified, providing an
immutable record of order progression.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`: Order this status snapshot belongs to. [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders).
- `status`
  > Current order status (e.g., 'pending', 'processing', 'shipped',
  > 'delivered', 'cancelled').
- `payment_status`
  > Payment processing status related to this order snapshot (e.g., 'paid',
  > 'pending', 'refunded').
- `total_amount`
  > Total amount paid for the order at the time of snapshot. Represents
  > financial value in base currency.
- `shipping_address`
  > Full shipping address associated with the order at the time of this
  > snapshot.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this order status snapshot was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this order status snapshot was last updated (typically
  > same as created_at for snapshot).
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this snapshot was marked for soft deletion (if applicable).

### `shopping_mall_order_cancellations`

Order cancellation requests initiated by customers or sellers.

Tracks all requests to cancel orders, including the reason, original
order details, and processing status. Cancellation requests follow a
workflow that may involve approval before the order is officially
canceled.

Each cancellation request corresponds to a specific order and contains
the reason provided by the customer or seller, along with the request
timestamp. The status field tracks progress through the validation and
processing workflow.

Requests can be in various states including pending (waiting for
verification), approved (cancellation validated), or rejected
(cancellation not permitted due to business rules or timing constraints).
This table enables tracking of the entire cancellation lifecycle.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing
cancellation request management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`: Reference to the original order. [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders).
- `cancellation_reason`: Reason provided by customer for cancellation request.
- `status`: Current status of the cancellation request: pending, approved, rejected.
- `requested_at`: Date and time when the cancellation request was submitted.
- `processed_at`: Date and time when the request was processed.
- `process_notes`: Internal notes about the cancellation processing decision.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the cancellation request was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last modification to the cancellation request.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp of when the cancellation request was soft deleted.

### `shopping_mall_order_refunds`

Records of customer-initiated refund requests with associated order and
payment details for financial reconciliation.

Each refund request is tied to a specific order and payment transaction,
tracking the refund amount, reason, and current status through the
approval workflow. Refund requests maintain historical records even after
order status changes or payment adjustments.

Refund status transitions follow business workflow rules: pending
(initiated), approved (processed), rejected (denied). The system
automatically initiates refunds when status moves to approved, triggering
payment gateway communication.

This table supports full audit trail capabilities including creation
timestamps and soft deletion for financial review purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_id`: Associated order's [shopping_mall_orders.id](#shopping_mall_orders).
- `payment_transaction_id`
  > Linked payment transaction's {@link
  > shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id}.
- `status`
  > Current refund status. Valid values: pending, approved, rejected. Follows
  > business workflow state transitions.
- `amount`: Refund amount in platform currency, matching payment transaction value.
- `reason`
  > Customer-specified reason for refund request. May include product issues
  > or service dissatisfaction.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when refund request was initiated by customer.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when refund status was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when refund record was soft-deleted for audit purposes.

### `shopping_mall_payment_transactions`

Payment transaction records tracking all attempts, including
success/failure status, gateway processing details, and associated order
information.

Stores complete history of payment processing for audit trail and
reconciliation. Each transaction links to an order and payment method,
enabling financial reporting, dispute resolution, and partial refund
tracking. Status transitions follow predefined workflow with explicit
change logging.

Transaction state changes are permanently recorded through the audit
trail, allowing recovery of historical data even if current status
changes. Gateway response logs provide critical detail for debugging
payment failures with external providers.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_order_id`
  > The order associated with this payment transaction. {@link

- `shopping_mall_payment_method_id`
  > The payment method used for this transaction. {@link
  > shopping_mall_payment_methods.id}.
- `status`
  > Current payment status. Valid values: pending, processing, completed,
  > failed, refunded.
- `amount`: Total amount processed, in platform currency.
- `transaction_id`
  > External transaction ID from the payment gateway for reconciliation with
  > third-party systems.
- `gateway_response`
  > Raw response received from the payment gateway including error details on
  > failures, stored for audit.
- `created_at`: Payment initiation timestamp when transaction was created.
- `updated_at`: Last status modification timestamp for transaction updates.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp when transaction record is marked inactive.

### `shopping_mall_payment_methods`

Configuration management for supported payment gateway integrations.

Stores system configurations for payment methods including API versions
and integration details. Each payment method (Stripe, PayPal, Alipay) has
unique configuration settings validated before use in payment processing.
This table enables dynamic configuration of payment gateways without
requiring code changes.

The name field identifies the payment method provider, while api_version
specifies the required gateway API version. Configuration stores
JSON-encoded settings for gateway integration including API keys, URLs,
and merchant IDs.

Transaction processing associates payment methods through foreign keys
while maintaining historical integrity. Soft delete supports
administrator management of gateway configurations without data loss.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`
  > Payment method name (e.g., 'Stripe', 'PayPal', 'Alipay'). Must be unique
  > across all payment methods.
- `api_version`
  > API version specification for the payment gateway. Used to validate
  > gateway compatibility during integration.
- `configuration`
  > JSON-encoded configuration string containing API keys, endpoints, and
  > integration parameters for the payment gateway.
- `status`
  > Current operational status of the payment method. Valid values: 'active',
  > 'inactive', 'pending'. Determines if method can be used for transactions.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when this payment method configuration was first created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when this payment method configuration was last modified.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this payment method configuration was marked for deletion
  > (soft delete). Supports audit trails and data recovery.

### `shopping_mall_refund_requests`

Tracks all refund requests submitted by customers including their status,
processing timeline, associated payment details, and final outcomes.

Stores refund requests at the point of creation, capturing the financial
details and customer's reason for the refund. Each request is uniquely
linked to a single payment transaction (one-to-one reference). The refund
workflow passes through several stages: pending (initial submission),
processing (under review), approved (ready for refund), rejected
(denied), and refunded (processed).

Systems can query refunds by status, date range, payment ID, or amount.
Refund amounts must match the payment transaction's amount limits. Soft
deletion allows refund tracking maintenance without data loss while
enabling fraud monitoring and audit trails.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_payment_transaction_id`
  > Associated payment transaction. {@link
  > shopping_mall_payment_transactions.id}
- `status`
  > Current refund processing status. Valid values: pending, processing,
  > approved, rejected, refunded.
- `reason`
  > Customer's explanation for requesting a refund, including specific issues
  > encountered with the purchase.
- `amount`
  > Refund amount requested in the payment's currency. Must not exceed
  > payment transaction amount.
- `requested_at`: Timestamp when the refund request was submitted by the customer.
- `processed_at`: Timestamp when processing of the refund request began.
- `completed_at`: Timestamp when the refund was successfully processed.
- `created_at`: Refund request creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Refund request last modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Refund request deletion timestamp (soft delete).

### `shopping_mall_reviews`

Product reviews and customer feedback records.

This table stores customer reviews for products, including ratings,
titles, and detailed feedback. Each review is associated with a specific
product and customer, allowing for independent management of feedback
without requiring parent entity context.

Reviews can be created, edited, and deleted by customers directly through
the application. The rating field provides a numeric score (1-5)
reflecting the customer's satisfaction with the product. Textual feedback
allows detailed descriptions of the customer's experience.

Unlike some entities where child records might be subsidiary, reviews
require independent management as customers might want to search all
reviews from a specific user, or filter reviews by rating across
products.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_product_id`
  > The product this review is associated with. {@link
  > shopping_mall_products.id}.
- `shopping_mall_customer_id`: Customer who created the review. [shopping_mall_customers.id](#shopping_mall_customers).
- `rating`
  > Numerical rating provided by customer (1-5). Higher values indicate
  > better satisfaction.
- `title`: Brief summary or title for the review. Optional but recommended.
- `body`: Detailed textual feedback from the customer about the product.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the review was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to the review.

### `shopping_mall_review_comments`

Comments made on product reviews by customers or sellers.

Stores user comments on product reviews to enable
discussion and feedback about the review itself.
Each comment is associated with a specific review
and can be made by either a customer or seller.

Comments remain attached to the review even if the review
is edited or deleted, providing historical context.
Users can reply to comments to create threaded discussions.
The comment content includes body field for textual
feedback. Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit
trails while allowing comment moderation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`: Review being commented on. [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews).
- `actor_type`: Type of actor making the comment (customer or seller).
- `body`: Text content of the comment.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the comment was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the comment was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the comment was soft-deleted (null if not deleted).

### `shopping_mall_review_votes`

Tracks user votes on product reviews to indicate helpfulness
(positive/negative).

Stores each vote as a separate record associated with a specific review.
Each vote can be marked as positive or negative to help other users
assess review quality.
Votes are tracked using session IDs for user tracking but not directly
tied to session IDs for this table.
Users can only vote once per review through their sessions, and vote
types can be revised.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`: Review being voted on. [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews)
- `vote_type`: Type of vote. Valid values: 'positive', 'negative'.
- `created_at`: When this vote was recorded.
- `updated_at`: When this vote was last modified.
- `deleted_at`: When this vote was soft-deleted (null if not deleted).

### `shopping_mall_review_moderation_logs`

Audit logs tracking all moderation actions taken on product reviews.

Captures details of review content modifications, flagging actions, and
moderator decisions. Each log entry records when and by whom a moderation
action was performed, with full audit trail capabilities for compliance
and review purposes.

Logs are never edited directly by users - they are append-only historical
records tied to the original review's state. The moderation log
references the review itself to provide context for why an action was
taken.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_mall_review_id`: Reviewed product review's [shopping_mall_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_reviews).
- `action`
  > Moderation action performed (e.g., 'flagged', 'hidden', 'approved',
  > 'edited').
- `reason`: Reason for the moderation action, including specific policy violations.
- `moderator_id`
  > Moderator's identity (references to shopping_mall_admins or
  > shopping_mall_seller_sessions.id).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of when the moderation action was performed.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last modification to this log entry.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the log entry was soft-deleted (for compliance audit
  > trails).

Customer registration must follow the service's security policy as documented in the Authentication_Requirements.md analysis file.

The registration process requires email verification before account activation, preventing unverified accounts from accessing premium features. The image data is retrieved from the ShoppingMallProductImage table in the database schema, which contains the image URL, dimensions, and other catalog presentation information. The operation uses the productCode to identify the parent product and imageCode to locate the specific image file within the product's image set.

This is a public endpoint with no authentication required, as product images are part of the public product catalog. There are no restrictions on who can access this image data, making it suitable for client-side product listings and catalog display systems.

operations.description:
Uploads a new image for a product using its unique product code. This operation allows sellers to add or replace product images in the product catalog. The unique product code (not ID) serves as the primary identifier for targeting the specific product. Only sellers authenticated with appropriate permissions can perform this operation. The request should include image metadata and the image file URL or data. This endpoint leverages the product image management capabilities defined in the ShoppingMall product management domain, ensuring proper categorization and association with the product.

Security: This operation requires 'seller' authorization to prevent unauthorized image uploads. Authentication token must be valid and associated with a seller account. The system validates that the seller owns the product being updated.

Business Logic: Product images are associated directly with the product entity. Each image record is created as a separate row in the database with a reference to the product code. The image metadata (like position, alt text, etc.) can be populated in the request body. There's no automatic file processing - the image file URL is simply stored.

Related Operations: Update product image (PUT /products/{productCode}/images/{imageId}), List product images (GET /products/{productCode}/images)

The operation supports contextual access to product variants and their technical details, allowing users to navigate from product catalog to full technical specifications without requiring complex joins. Integrated with the product catalog system, this operation ensures consistency between listings and technical data. Specification information is maintained independently from product catalog details but remains tightly coupled for up-to-date product presentation across the platform. The system ensures that only active and valid product specifications are exposed through this endpoint.

This operation provides product technical data intended for customer-facing consumption, making it accessible to authenticated users. A low-level authentication mechanism ensures that only valid users can access product details, while trading off additional role-based authorization to reduce endpoint complexity. The operation does not require special permissions as technical product specifications are generally non-sensitive information that is meant for product discovery and user decision-making.

operations.description:
Create a new order cancellation request for an existing shopping order. This operation allows authenticated customers to initiate the cancellation of an order that has not yet been processed. The order must be in a cancellable state, and cancellation requests are subject to specific business rules based on the order's current status, time elapsed since purchase, and the products involved.

Security: Only the customer who placed the order can initiate cancellations, with the customer's identity automatically determined from the JWT authentication token. The system validates that the order belongs to the requesting customer and that it meets the cancellation criteria (orders cannot be cancelled once processing has begun, typically after 24 hours or if inventory has been allocated). This operation is part of the main order management workflow and integrates with the order status tracking system.

Business rules: Cancellation requests are only allowed for active orders (status: 'pending' or 'processing') within 24 hours of purchase. The system automatically checks these conditions and rejects requests that don't comply. Upon success, the order status is updated to 'cancelled' and an order cancellation record is created in the database. Related operations include order status view (GET /orders/{orderCode}) and cancellation status check (GET /orders/{orderCode}/cancellations).

This operation uses the code-based identifier for the order to create a human-readable and URL-friendly path structure. The order code is globally unique across all orders, allowing unambiguous identification regardless of other attributes. The parameter definition aligns with the database schema's @@unique([code]) constraint for the order entity, ensuring reliable identification of the target order.

Security considerations require this endpoint to be accessible only to authenticated administrators with elevated privileges. The operation returns summary metrics without exposing sensitive authentication details such as token values or authentication credentials.

responseBody.description: Comprehensive authentication status dashboard metrics for platform administrators

operations.name: index

operations.description:
This operation retrieves email verification analytics data including verification success rates, average token validity duration, and verification failure patterns. The results are derived from the shopping_mall_email_verification_tokens database table, which stores token-related data including timestamps, email addresses, and verification status.

The analytics provide valuable insights for administrators to monitor the email verification system's performance, identify trends, and optimize the verification process. Security considerations require administrative privileges to access this endpoint, ensuring that only trusted personnel can view sensitive analytics data.

This endpoint uses a GET method for retrieving the analytics, avoiding request bodies as these are typically reserved for complex searches. The response format is designed to support comprehensive analytics viewing, providing both summary metrics and detailed breakdowns where applicable.

responseBody.description: Analytics data for email verification tokens including verification rates, success metrics, and token usage patterns.

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Allows authenticated users to perform complex product searches with advanced filtering across multiple product attributes, categories, and specifications. This endpoint utilizes the Products database model to support full-text search, category-based filtering, price ranges, and attribute-based queries including color, size, material, and variant-specific details. The search operation supports pagination, sorting options, and comprehensive filtering capabilities to provide an optimized shopping experience for customers and sellers. Implementation leverages the shopping_mall_products and shopping_mall_product_specs tables with join operations for full attribute coverage.

Security considerations include authentication using the 'customer' actor with appropriate permissions. Only authenticated customers can access product search functionality. The endpoint does not require any sensitive data access or authorization beyond basic user authentication. This search endpoint can be used in conjunction with other product-related operations such as product detail retrieval (GET /products/{productId}) and product category browsing (GET /categories/{categoryId}).
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Advanced search parameters including filters, sorting options, and pagination settings

responseBody.description: Paginated results of product summaries with essential information for catalog display

operations.description:
Return enriched product details including product information, associated seller details, and category hierarchy.

This operation retrieves a product with additional context information from its associated tables, providing a single comprehensive response rather than requiring multiple API calls. The enriched product includes all necessary product details plus detailed seller information and the full category hierarchy.

The response is designed for optimal performance by pre-joining data related to the product, eliminating the need for multiple client-side API calls to get complete product information. This data structure combines information from the products, sellers, and categories tables into a single unified object.

This endpoint is available to all users without authentication and returns only publicly viewable product information, which aligns with the platform's core functionality for product discovery and browsing.

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated low stock trend analysis across inventory items to identify declining stock patterns and optimize restocking strategies. This operation aggregates data from the low_stock_alerts and inventory_logs tables to provide time-based inventory trend analysis without retrieving individual stock records.

The trend analysis computes weekly stock level changes, alert frequencies, and stock-out probabilities by analyzing historical inventory logs and alert records. Results help inventory managers identify products that are consistently running low and prioritize procurement efforts.

Security considerations: This endpoint is restricted to administrative users who require inventory analytics for business operations. Unauthorized access attempts are logged for security monitoring and audit purposes. The response includes only trend summaries without sensitive raw inventory data to maintain data privacy.

responseBody.description: Paginated trend summaries including date ranges, stock levels, and alert frequencies for inventory analysis

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: Product category hierarchy must be established before creating low stock alert configurations

operations.description: Retrieves a comprehensive overview of inventory status across all product variants for platform administrators, aggregating current stock levels, low stock alert status, and category-level inventory summaries. This operation is specifically designed for administrative dashboard use cases to support inventory management decisions across the shopping mall platform. The data is derived from multiple schema entities including shopping_mall_variant_inventories, shopping_mall_product_categories, and shopping_mall_low_stock_alerts, providing both real-time counts and alert status indicators. This summary is optimized for rapid analysis with key metrics prioritized for dashboard display, including current stock levels, minimum threshold values, and immediate restocking priorities. The implementation executes a SQL join across inventory data, product categories, and alert configurations to provide a holistic view without requiring additional API calls for contextual information.

responseBody.description: Aggregated inventory summary with category-level metrics and low stock alert indicators for dashboard display

operations.name: inventoryOverview

operations.description:
Perform a search through product inventory items with filtering, pagination, and sorting capabilities. This operation accesses the shopping_mall_variant_inventories database schema to retrieve current inventory status across all product variants, supporting queries by product name, category, stock levels, and location. The endpoint implements a robust search mechanism that optimizes for performance by leveraging existing database indexes on inventory fields. Security considerations include mandatory authentication to prevent unauthorized inventory checks, with access restricted to authenticated business users who have valid roles. The response includes inventory summaries optimized for list views, containing only essential field data to reduce payload size. This operation integrates with the shopping_mall_variant_inventories model and related product information tables to provide complete inventory context.

Implementation notes: This endpoint serves as a core business operation for monitoring stock levels across the platform. It returns inventory summaries rather than full entity details to optimize performance for a high-frequency search operation. The inventory search capabilities include filtering by product name substring matching, category IDs, and minimum quantity thresholds. Response pagination is implemented to handle potentially large inventory datasets efficiently.

Technical integration: This operation uses the shopping_mall_variant_inventories table as the primary data source, with joins to product categories and variants to enrich the search results. The search functionality is implemented using database-level filtering and ordering rather than application-level processing.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for inventory filtering

responseBody.description: Paginated list of inventory item summaries with essential stock information

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated review rating analytics across all products with filtering and sorting capabilities. This operation computes statistical metrics including average ratings, helpfulness scores, review distribution, and sentiment patterns by analyzing data from the ShoppingMallReview and ShoppingMallReviewVote tables. The endpoint provides business intelligence for platform administrators to monitor product performance, customer satisfaction trends, and review quality metrics.

Implementation note: This statistical aggregation executes multiple GROUP BY operations to calculate metrics including: SELECT product_id, AVG(rating) AS avg_rating, COUNT(*) AS review_count, AVG(vote_helpful) AS avg_vote, MAX(created_at) AS last_review_date FROM shopping_mall_reviews
LEFT JOIN shopping_mall_review_votes ON shopping_mall_reviews.id = shopping_mall_review_votes.review_id GROUP BY product_id ORDER BY avg_rating DESC LIMIT 50

Security: Restricted to admin actors only. The operation uses administrative authentication to ensure sensitive business analytics remain confidential. No user-modifiable data is affected by this read-only operation.

responseBody.description: Paginated collection of summary review analytics with average ratings, vote statistics, and review distribution metrics

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieve the moderation dashboard data for product reviews, providing aggregated statistics and pending review items for administrative oversight. This operation serves business requirements where platform moderators need an at-a-glance view of review activity, including newly submitted reviews awaiting approval, flagged reviews, and overall moderation metrics.

The dashboard combines data from multiple related entities: customer reviews (shopping_mall_reviews), user votes (shopping_mall_review_votes), and product relationships (shopping_mall_products). It aggregates key moderation metrics such as pending reviews count, average sentiment score, and flagging rates to provide actionable insights for platform administrators.

Security considerations include strict authorization for admin-level access only. The operation implements rate limiting for moderation activities and excludes sensitive user information in the response. This endpoint supports the business requirement for efficient content moderation without requiring multiple API calls to gather dashboard metrics.

responseBody.description: Dashboard summary containing moderation metrics and pending review items

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Retrieves a filtered list of product reviews from the shopping platform. This endpoint operates against the shopping_mall_reviews table in the database schema, providing comprehensive search capabilities for customers and sellers to find relevant reviews based on various criteria including product ID, rating range, review status, and creation date filters.

The operation supports advanced pagination with customizable page sizes, sorting options for review date, rating, and relevance, and flexible filtering to narrow results by product, user, and status. This implementation directly reflects the review search requirements outlined in continuous product development workflows.

Security considerations include mandatory user authentication for all requests, ensuring that only authenticated customers can access review data. The endpoint includes robust validation for search parameters to prevent invalid queries and implements appropriate rate limiting to maintain service stability during high traffic periods. The underlying database schema defines review data constraints that directly inform this endpoint's behavior and response structure.
operations.name: index

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering reviews

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary information matching search criteria

prerequisites.description: Product must exist before it can be referenced in reviews. The product must be created via POST /shoppingMall/seller/products to establish a valid product_id for review searches.

applications.

email.description:
Email address for authentication and communication.

Validated against RFC 5322 email format standards to prevent invalid addresses. The system verifies email uniqueness against existing customer records. This field is mandatory for account creation and must be a valid business email format to ensure communication reliability.

The email serves as the primary username for login and is used in all security communications including account verification and password resets. Email validation is a critical security measure to prevent fake accounts and ensure the account belongs to a valid user.

username.description:
Unique username for customer identification.

Validated against the shopping_mall_customers table to ensure uniqueness before account creation. This field serves as the display name in the system's front-end interfaces and is not used for authentication.

Customer must provide a unique username during registration. The system enforces this uniqueness to prevent duplicate identities and improve user experience through personalized identification.

IShoppingMallCustomer.IJoin.description: Request DTO for new customer account registration with session context. Contains all necessary information for account creation including authentication credentials, unique username, and mandatory session context fields (href, referrer) for connection tracking

IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized.description:
Mandatory session details after successful admin authentication and account creation operations. Contains the unique administrative account identifier and authentication token necessary for maintaining access.

The ID field is a UUID that corresponds to the primary key of the shopping_mall_admins table. This identifier is used to associate subsequent API requests with the specific admin account.

The token field contains the JWT access token and its associated metadata. This token is essential for all subsequent authenticated API calls and is automatically generated by the authentication system. It expires after a certain period and can be refreshed using the /auth/admin/refresh endpoint.

This schema is the standard response format for all admin authentication operations, including account creation (join) and login. It does not include sensitive fields like password, as these are managed server-side.

id.description: Unique identifier for the admin account. Corresponds to the primary key in shopping_mall_admins table.

email.description:
Official email address associated with the administrator account.

This email is used for all system communications, login verification, and administrative notifications. The email address must follow RFC 5322 format standards to ensure proper system processing.

In the database schema, this maps to the `email` field in shopping_mall_admins which has a unique constraint and is required for account creation.

name.description:
Primary name associated with the administrator account.

This field contains the administrator's full name or preferred name for display purposes. Name length is limited to 100 characters to prevent abuse and maintain usability across system interfaces.

The database schema implementation uses this field for user display purposes without additional processing.

phone.description:
Contact phone number for the administrator.

This optional field allows administrators to provide their contact information for emergency communications or verification purposes. The phone number should be in E.164 format for international compatibility.

In the database schema, this field is stored as a string in phone format and allows null for privacy preferences or incomplete profile information.

oneOf.description:
Administrative role assigned to the account.

This role determines the permissions and capabilities available to the administrator within the system. The system supports three predefined role types with strictly defined access levels.

The database schema uses this field to implement role-based access control (RBAC) with fixed enum values.

role.description:
Administrative role assigned to the account.

This role determines the permissions and capabilities available to the administrator within the system. The system supports three predefined role types with strictly defined access levels.
